data.title: Iberdrola completes 97.5-MW wind farm repowering in Spain
data.description:
November 20 (Renewables Now) - Spanish utility Iberdrola SA has finalised the repowering of its Isabela and Molar del Molinar wind farms in the Castile-La Mancha region, maintaining their capacity at 97.5 MW with fewer turbines.

The two wind farms are more than two decades old and are some of the first that Iberdrola installed in Spain. Their repowering involved replacing 139 turbines with 22 new machines, which is expected to increase electricity production by around 30%, the utility said.

At the 49.5-MW Molar del Molinar wind farm in Penas de San Pedro, Iberdrola replaced 75 turbines rated at 660 kW each with 11 Vestas machines of 4.5 MW apiece.

At the 48-MW Isabela wind farm, near Casas de Lazaro and Penascosa, the company took down 64 turbines rated at 750 kW to add 11 new machines, six rated at 4.5 MW and five at 4.2 MW.

The two renovated wind farms are expected to generate enough electricity to meet the annual consumption of more than 55,500 households, Iberdrola said.

Construction at Isabel and Molar del Molinar began in 2024. The projects received a combined EUR 22.71 million (USD 24.9m) in support from the Spanish state under the Circular Repowering programme, managed by the Institute for Energy Diversification and Saving (IDAE).

During the works, Iberdrola hired EnergyLoop, a recycling company established by Iberdrola Ventures Perseo and FCC Ambito, to process the decommissioned turbine blades. The operation involved removing 139 turbines and 417 blades, with more than 800 tonnes of material treated for recovery and recycling.

(EUR 1.0 = USD 1.098)

data.title: KIMPTON SURFCOMBER HOTEL DEEPENS ITS CONNECTION TO THE ARTS WITH A CELEBRATION OF LOCAL CREATIVITY FOR MIAMI ART WEEK 2026
data.description:
From immersive installations and hands-on art experiences to live painting and art-inspired culinary offerings, the South Beach hotel puts local talent in the spotlight

MIAMI, Nov. 20, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- At Kimpton Surfcomber Hotel, art isn't reserved for one week of the year. From its historic Art Deco roots to its ongoing collaborations with local artists, creativity is woven into the essence of the oceanfront South Beach hotel. This Miami Art Week, Surfcomber is building on that legacy with a special lineup of experiences celebrating the talent and artistic spirit of its local community.

From a striking new lobby installation to interactive art experiences at its newly renovated signature restaurant, The Social Club, and a colorful showcase at the Cabanas at its newly opened Solei Beach Club, the programming brings creativity to every corner of the property. Paired with imaginative culinary and cocktail offerings and a special shopping pop-up, the celebration invites guests and locals to experience art in unexpected ways against the backdrop of Surfcomber's idyllic oceanfront setting.

"Art has always been part of Surfcomber's identity, and our connection to Miami's creative community extends far beyond Art Week," said Mohan Koka, General Manager of Kimpton Surfcomber Hotel. "Over the years, we've had the privilege of working with some incredibly talented local artists, and we love finding new ways to bring their creativity into the guest experience. This year's celebration is all about building on those relationships, giving artists a platform to share their work and inviting visitors to experience a side of Miami's art scene they might not otherwise discover."

This year's programming brings together Miami-born artist Alex Nuñez, collage artist Kimberly Welbaum—whose cutmepasteme works have adorned the walls of The Social Club since its renovation—and Miami-based painter Jonathan Pedigo. Together, their distinct artistic styles will take center stage across the property, inviting guests to explore thought-provoking installations, get creative alongside the artists, witness live painting in action and even take home a limited-edition piece of Surfcomber's Art Week celebration.

A Closer Look at Surfcomber's Miami Art Week Programming

No Vacancy, Miami Beach: Alex Nuñez's You Cannot Step into the Same Ocean TwiceAs part of the City of Miami Beach's No Vacancy public art program, Surfcomber will welcome Miami-born artist Alex Nuñez for an immersive installation on display from November 12 through December 19. Titled You Cannot Step into the Same Ocean Twice, the exhibition transforms The Nook, the hotel's cozy lobby corner, into an otherworldly environment featuring printed aluminum palms, paintings and works on paper, anchored by an iridescent portal that shifts with the changing light. The installation invites visitors to experience a familiar coastal landscape through an entirely new lens, offering a moment of discovery just steps from the energy of South Beach.

A Celebration of Collage at The Social ClubFrom November 29 through December 7, Surfcomber's newly renovated signature restaurant, The Social Club, will become a playground for creativity in collaboration with Miami-based collage artist Kimberly Welbaum, the talent behind cutmepasteme. A fixture of The Social Club's artistic identity since its renovation, Welbaum's vibrant, layered works have become part of the restaurant's everyday atmosphere. For Miami Art Week, the hotel is taking that relationship beyond the walls, inviting guests to engage directly with the artist and her creative process through interactive installations, hands-on experiences and exclusive, limited-edition artwork.

  • Your Mark of Art: From November 29 through December 5, guests dining at The Social Club can add their own artistic flair to an interactive art experience led by Kimberly Welbaum. Through hand-cut fragments, color becomes a language for emotion. Together, individual feelings become one collective work of art. Guests are invited to browse a collection of colorful fragments, select the pieces that speak to them and contribute their own arrangement to the evolving artwork. Following Miami Art Week, Welbaum will carefully preserve and refine the individual contributions, bringing them together into a finished, signed original artwork—a one-of-a-kind creation shaped by the guests who helped bring it to life. Click HERE to reserve your table for your mark of art.
  • Cut, Paste & Cocktails: On December 5, from 3 to 5 p.m., Welbaum will lead an intimate collage workshop where guests can explore her signature techniques, create their own artwork and enjoy unlimited Sarti and Aperol Spritz cocktails alongside charcuterie. Participants will leave with their finished creations and a take-home art kit. Space is limited to 30 guests. Click HERE to purchase tickets.
  • A Piece of Art Week to Take Home: To commemorate the collaboration, Welbaum has created 200 individually signed, limited-edition 8-by-10-inch art prints exclusively for Surfcomber. These special keepsakes will be placed in guest rooms during Miami Art Week, offering visitors a chance to bring a piece of the hotel's artistic spirit home.

Flavor of Miami: Jonathan Pedigo at Solei Beach ClubFrom November 30 through December 7, the new Cabanas at Solei Beach Club will be transformed into a vibrant showcase of local artistry with Flavor of Miami, a collaboration with Miami-based artist Jonathan Pedigo and The Curation Department, a creative platform connecting artists with spaces and audiences through curated art experiences. Known for his bold use of color, expressive compositions and playful visual storytelling, Pedigo brings a distinctly energetic aesthetic to the oceanfront setting, with a selection of his works displayed throughout the cabanas alongside art-inspired cocktails handcrafted by Solei Beach Club's expert mixologists. Guests can explore the pieces at their own pace, with QR codes offering a closer look at the artist and the inspiration behind his work. Cabanas are available to rent through ResortPass.

On Friday, December 4, Pedigo will put an artistic spin on Surfcomber's signature Social Hour with a special live painting experience from 5 to 7 p.m., open to hotel guests and the public alike. Visitors can settle in with a drink in hand and watch as the artist transforms a blank canvas into an original work of art, bringing a little extra color and creativity to the hotel's beloved evening ritual—all against the backdrop of its idyllic oceanfront setting. For more details and to RSVP, click here.

The Blue Dynasty Experience: Where Art Meets the MenuFrom November 30 through December 7, The Social Club will take Miami Art Week indulgence to new heights with the introduction of the Blue Dynasty Experience, an extravagant, limited-time culinary creation from Executive Chef Gastón Javier. Inspired by Johnnie Walker Blue Label, the experience puts a luxurious spin on the classic burger, featuring American Wagyu, aged Alpine cheese, Blue Label bacon jam and winter black truffle, all nestled in a buttery brioche roll. Served alongside duck-fat pomme pavé finished with truffle sea salt and paired with a 2 oz pour of Johnnie Walker Blue Label, the $125 experience offers a decidedly decadent way to savor Miami Art Week.

A Touch of Sparkle: Kendra Scott Holiday Pop-UpRounding out Kimpton Surfcomber's Miami Art Week festivities with a fashionable flourish, jewelry and lifestyle brand Kendra Scott will bring its signature style to the hotel lobby for a special one-day shopping experience on Saturday, December 5, from 10 a.m. to 5 p.m. Celebrating fashion as another form of creative expression, the pop-up invites guests and locals to explore and shop the brand's newest collection, offering the perfect opportunity to discover a statement piece of their own amid the week's artistic inspiration.

"Miami Art Week is an incredible time to explore the city, but we also wanted to create moments that invite people to slow down and enjoy the art in a more personal way," said Victoria Palacio, Marketing Manager of Kimpton Surfcomber Hotel. "There's something special about sitting down for a meal and realizing you can contribute to the artwork around you, or watching an artist bring a painting to life while you're enjoying the ocean breeze. Those are the kinds of experiences we hope people take away from their time at Surfcomber."

With 200 feet of oceanfront in the heart of South Beach, Kimpton Surfcomber Hotel offers an inviting escape from the whirlwind of Miami Art Week without missing a moment of the excitement. Between gallery hopping and art-filled afternoons, visitors can settle into the laid-back coastal atmosphere of the newly opened Solei Beach Club, inspired by the sun-drenched shores of Spain, or linger over South of France-inspired cuisine at the newly renovated The Social Club. Whether stopping in for a creative experience, gathering with friends over a leisurely meal or making a weekend of it, Surfcomber brings together the art, energy and easygoing spirit that make Miami Beach unlike anywhere else.

For more information on Surfcomber's Miami Art Week programming, visit surfcomber.com/hotels-on-collins-ave/art-basel-miami. For hotel reservations, visit surfcomber.com.

data.title: Post-Festive Hiring: Employers Shift Focus From Volume To Workforce Readiness
data.description:
With temporary hiring projected to grow 15–20 per cent in 2026, companies are focusing on faster onboarding, targeted incentives and employee experience to manage peak demand

India's festive shopping season offers employers an opportunity to assess how effectively their workforce strategies respond to rising demand. For companies across retail, e-commerce, quick commerce and logistics, the period puts recruitment, onboarding, compensation and employee engagement practices to the test, with lessons extending to future hiring cycles.

TeamLease Services' Festive Season Workforce Report 2026: The Great Indian Festive Rush projected temporary hiring growth of 15–20 per cent in 2026. Festive e-commerce gross merchandise value crossed Rs 1.2 lakh crore in 2025, up about 27 per cent from 2024, while quick commerce increased its share of festive spending to 12 per cent from 8 per cent.

The report draws on anonymised employment records of about 60,000 frontline associates across consumer durables, organised retail, e-commerce, quick commerce, logistics and fast-moving consumer goods (FMCG). Its findings point to a shift in workforce planning from hiring at scale to ensuring employees are prepared to contribute quickly during peak periods.

Hiring For Peak Readiness

"The festive hiring season continues to evolve beyond volume hiring to precision hiring," said Balasubramanian A, senior vice president and business head at TeamLease Services.

The report identifies candidate readiness, basic digital literacy and immediate productivity as important considerations in seasonal recruitment. Employers are increasingly looking at advance talent pools, digital onboarding, cross-training and deployment closer to dark stores and fulfilment centres to help employees become productive faster.

Shailesh Khanna, business leader at ManpowerGroup India, said workforce planning was moving from reactive volume hiring towards a more predictive and agile model.

"The focus is no longer just on filling large numbers of temporary positions, but on leveraging predictive hiring, digital onboarding, talent reusability, and agile deployment to meet peak demand faster while improving speed-to-productivity, workforce quality, and operational efficiency," Khanna said.

This approach places greater emphasis on preparing employees for their roles rather than measuring hiring success solely by the number of positions filled. Faster onboarding and targeted training can help businesses reduce the time between recruitment and deployment, while cross-training can give employers greater flexibility in allocating staff across functions.

Incentives And Compensation Take Centre Stage

Compensation is another important element of festive workforce planning. TeamLease identifies several variable-pay mechanisms, including attendance and tenure-completion bonuses, productivity-linked rewards, referral incentives, fuel reimbursement for delivery workers and additional pay for night shifts.

The report placed median monthly cost to company (CTC) for frontline festive workers at Rs 20,525 in the second half of 2025, compared with Rs 20,282 a year earlier. It projected an 8–10 per cent increase in CTC in the second half of 2026. These projections should be distinguished from actual post-season outcomes.

For employers, incentives can help attract workers for time-bound assignments and encourage employees to complete seasonal contracts. Their effectiveness, however, depends on clear eligibility criteria, reliable payments and compensation structures that reflect the requirements of the role.

Sruti Mishra, head of talent acquisition at ZEISS India, said a combination of competitive pay, performance-linked incentives and practical employee benefits helped the company support workforce continuity.

"Production-yield-linked incentives reinforce quality and productivity, while attendance and tenure-completion bonuses reduce absenteeism and encourage employees to complete their training or tenure," Mishra said.

She added that commuting support, complimentary meals and uniforms also helped strengthen employee engagement and retention.

Mishra clarified that ZEISS's hiring is primarily driven by business requirements rather than festive demand. Its practices nevertheless illustrate how employers can use a combination of compensation, workplace benefits and structured training to support employees during periods of higher operational requirements.

Training And Career Pathways Beyond Seasonal Hiring

The post-festive period also raises questions about how employers can retain the skills and experience developed during temporary hiring cycles. For companies, seasonal recruitment can offer an opportunity to identify workers who may be suitable for longer-term roles, provided business requirements and individual performance align.

Khanna said employers were increasingly treating seasonal workers as an extension of their longer-term workforce strategy. Technology-enabled onboarding, bite-sized digital learning, real-time performance management and pathways to permanent employment were among the practices helping organisations improve job readiness and sustain engagement.

At ZEISS India, Mishra said temporary staff and apprentices undergo a structured 30-day induction and ongoing training. Apprentices may progress to fixed-term contracts on the company's payroll and subsequently to full-time employment, subject to performance and business needs.

The company also tracks productivity, attendance, absenteeism and monthly attrition, while regular employee interactions and a grievance-handling mechanism provide channels to identify and address workplace concerns.

These practices show how workforce planning can extend beyond immediate staffing requirements. Training, employee feedback and clearly defined career pathways can help employers build a more reliable talent pipeline while giving workers greater clarity about future opportunities.

Employee Well-Being In Focus

Workforce readiness also depends on the quality of the employee experience. ManpowerGroup's Global Talent Barometer 2026: India Report and Key Findings, based on a survey of 1,025 workers in India conducted between 1 September and 1 October 2025, found that 75 per cent of Indian workers reported experiencing burnout. The findings are not specific to festive employment but provide broader context on employee well-being.

The report recorded a well-being score of 68 per cent among blue-collar workers, compared with 77 per cent for the Indian workforce overall. Support for work-life balance stood at 79 per cent among blue-collar workers and 78 per cent among essential frontline workers, against 88 per cent among executives and senior leaders.

These differences make employee support an important consideration when companies review their seasonal workforce strategies. Shift planning, adequate rest, commuting arrangements, overtime management and clear communication around incentives can influence how employees experience periods of heightened demand.

Khanna said employers were increasingly recognising that festive-season performance depended not only on adding headcount but also on managing workforce fatigue. He pointed to structured overtime management, flexible scheduling and enhanced rewards as approaches being used to balance operational requirements with employee well-being.

He added that staffing partners were increasingly being assessed on measures such as attendance, retention, productivity and worker well-being, alongside fulfilment rates.

Building A More Prepared Workforce

The post-festive period allows HR leaders to evaluate which workforce practices delivered results and where planning can improve. Companies can review recruitment timelines, onboarding effectiveness, incentive structures, absenteeism, employee feedback and the proportion of temporary workers offered continued employment.

The lessons may extend beyond the festive season. Advance talent pools, skills-based deployment, transparent compensation and better shift planning can help businesses respond to future demand peaks while improving the employee experience.

Ultimately, festive workforce planning is not just about having enough people during the busiest weeks of the year. It is about ensuring employees are prepared for their roles, supported during periods of high demand and given a clear understanding of their compensation and employment opportunities.

data.title: ICE Canola Holding to Up One Day, Down the Next Pattern
data.description:
WINNIPEG, Manitoba--Intercontinental Exchange canola futures continued to teeter-totter late Friday morning, with prices falling back.

The rangebound Canadian oilseed was on course to hold true to its pattern this week of up one day and down the next.

"We need fresh demand at these levels," a trader said, noting that export buyers haven't stepped up lately.

The trader also said the U.S. markets "are soft and volatile." He added that if crude oil prices would stabilize, that would lead to stability for canola and other vegetable oils.

Declines in crude oil were accelerating Friday, putting greater pressure on the veg oils. That weighed on Chicago soyoil, European rapeseed and Malaysian palm oil. However, Chicago soybeans and soymeal were still on the rise.

The forecast for canola ending stocks in 2026-27 were trimmed by 100,000 metric tons by Agriculture and Agri-Food Canada in its November supply and demand report. AAFC now expects the carryout to be 1.87 million metric tons, versus 1.89 million in 2025-26.

Statistics Canada will update its crop estimates in its net production report on Dec. 4.

The Canadian Grain Commission said canola exports for the week ended Nov. 15 dropped 54% at 141,000 metric tons. However, domestic use on the week rose 29% at 246,300 metric tons.

The Canadian dollar was virtually unchanged late Friday morning with the loonie at 69.84 U.S. cents.

New Loan Facilities

Kropz Plc (AIM: KRPZ), an emerging African phosphate producer and developer, announces that Kropz Elandsfontein (Pty) Ltd (“Elandsfontein”) and Ubuntu-Botho Investments (Pty) Ltd (“UBI”) (together the “Parties”) have agreed to a ZAR 370 million (approximately US$ 22.5 million) loan facility (the “First Loan”), and further announces that Elandsfontein and ARC Fund (“ARC”) have agreed to a ZAR 165 million (approximately US$ 10.0 million) loan facility (the “Second Loan”, and together with the Loan, the “Loans”), which constitute related party transactions.

The First Loan

Elandsfontein and UBI have agreed terms for a demand loan facility of ZAR 370 million (approximately US$ 22.5 million). Interest is payable on the Loan at the South African prime overdraft interest rate plus 6%, nominal per annum and compounded monthly. The Loan is repayable on the earlier of a date as agreed between the Parties or on demand from UBI, on no less than 15 business days' notice. There is no fixed repayment term and the First Loan may be drawn until 31 March 2028, with each drawdown at UBI's sole discretion. The First Loan may be repaid at any time on two business days' notice without penalty. No fees are payable and no warrants or conversion rights have been granted in connection with the First Loan. The First Loan is to fund Elandsfontein's cashflow and operational requirements. No amount has yet been drawn.

As announced on 21 May 2025 and 28 May 2025, Kropz SA (Pty) Ltd (“Kropz SA”) has issued a Guarantee, Security Cession and Pledge in favour of ARC, and Kropz Plc has issued a Limited Indemnity, Security Cession and Pledge in favour of ARC for all current and future loan facilities made to Elandsfontein, which are applicable to the Loans. As announced on 15 July 2026, these agreements were extended by the parties in favour of UBI as the first ranking priority (through an omnibus agreement), and in favour of ARC as the second ranking priority, issued by Kropz SA for all current and future loan facilities of Kropz Elandsfontein. That ranking is unchanged and no new security documents are being entered into in connection with the Loans.

The Company will update the market on drawdown of the Loan in due course.

The Second Loan

Elandsfontein and ARC have agreed terms for a demand loan facility of ZAR 165 million (approximately US$ 10.0 million). Interest is payable on the Second Loan at the South African prime overdraft interest rate plus 6%, nominal per annum and compounded monthly. The Second Loan is repayable on the earlier of a date as agreed between Elandsfontein and ARC or on demand from ARC, on no less than 15 business days' notice. There is no fixed repayment term and the Second Loan may be drawn until 31 March 2028, with each drawdown at ARC's sole discretion. Drawdown is also conditional on certain approvals from ARC's investors, which must be given before any drawdown. The Second Loan may be repaid at any time on two business days' notice without penalty. No fees are payable and no warrants or conversion rights have been granted in connection with the Second Loan. The Second Loan is to fund capital expenditure. No amount has yet been drawn.

The Company will update the market on drawdown of the Second Loan in due course.

UBI is the indirect controlling shareholder of ARC, and consequently the Loans are related party transactions pursuant to Rule 13 of the AIM Rules for Companies. data.title: Mongolian president's resignation sets stage for early election
data.description:
Key points:
  • Parliament approves resignation, election due in four months
  • Khurelsukh said he stepped down to clear his name
  • Turmoil lifts lid on divisions in coal-rich nation

Mongolia's parliament approved the resignation of Khurelsukh Ukhnaa as president on Thursday, two days after he asked to step down amid accusations by rivals of corruption, setting the stage for an early election.

Khurelsukh's resignation — which he said was to allow an investigation and clear his name — is the first time a sitting Mongolian president has quit before completing their term, and lifted the lid on political infighting in the coal-rich nation.

The opposition Democratic Party started calling for Khurelsukh to go after the capital's former mayor said in a livestream on his Facebook page on Saturday there was corruption involved in a railway project.

The ex-mayor, Nyambaatar Khishgee, is also a former justice minister and a member of a rival faction in the ruling Mongolian People's Party, with which Khurelsukh has long been affiliated.

"I will bring those who are defaming me before the relevant authorities and have my honour restored," Khurelsukh said during a press briefing announcing his resignation on Tuesday, according to the state Montsame news agency.

"I have never lied, stole or deceived anyone," he added.

His departure showed the depth of divisions and animosity in Mongolian politics, said Xu Tianchen, a senior analyst at the Economist Intelligence Unit.

"Not only is there intense hostility between the ruling Mongolian People's Party and the opposition Democratic Party, but there are also factional struggles within the Mongolian People's Party itself," Xu said.

Parliament, which under Mongolian law must approve the resignation of a president, did so with 96 of the 104 members present voting in favour, Montsame reported.

The State Great Khural assembly must now call an election in four months, with parliament speaker, Byambatsogt Sandag, exercising presidential powers in the meantime.

Anger over accusations of corruption has repeatedly boiled over into street protests in recent years.

In June 2025, then Prime Minister L. Oyun-Erdene stepped down after losing parliamentary support following corruption allegations that he denied.

His successor, Zandanshatar Gombojav, resigned in March 2026 amid a parliamentary boycott by the opposition party and mounting infighting within the MPP.

Khurelsukh himself also resigned as prime minister in 2021 following protests over the government's handling of the COVID-19 pandemic. He was elected president later that same year.

data.title: Second US judge blocks construction of Trump arch project
data.description:
By Jan Wolfe

A federal judge in Alexandria, Virginia on Friday said she would issue a preliminary injunction blocking construction of President Donald Trump’s proposed triumphal arch, saying during a hearing that it was a “rushed job” that lacked a legal basis.

Earlier this month, US District Judge Tanya Chutkan in Washington issued a separate order temporarily blocking construction of the proposed 250-foot arch near Arlington National Cemetery. The rulings are the latest setbacks for one of Trump's many efforts to leave a lasting architectural mark on the nation’s capital.

The White House did not immediately comment. Trump has faced significant pushback from the judiciary against projects he has undertaken in Washington during his second term, which have included a White House ballroom project, a renovation of the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool and a proposed championship-level golf course two miles from the White House.

data.description:

  • Fourteen out of 22 analysts covering the stock rate it ‘Hold’, while eight rate the stock ‘Buy’ or ‘Strong Buy’, according to Koyfin. 
  • The company lowered its fiscal 2026 sales growth forecast to roughly flat from 1% to 1.5% growth and cut its adjusted EPS and operating-margin outlooks.

Gap Inc. (GAP) shares drew investor attention on Friday after multiple analysts lowered their price targets on the retailer following its third-quarter results.

UBS lowered its price target on Gap to $36 from $42 and kept a ‘Buy’ rating on the shares, according to The Fly. The firm sees Gap delivering average annual earnings-per-share (EPS) growth of 18% over the next two years, supported by continued strength at the Gap brand, an Old Navy recovery and operating efficiencies, The Fly reported.

GAP shares were trading above 16% at the time of writing.

Analysts Flag Brand Challenges, Consumer Pressure

BMO Capital lowered its price target on Gap to $21 from $24 while maintaining a 'Market Perform' rating, according to The Fly. The firm said that despite another strong quarter from the Gap brand, challenges across the company's other brands continue to weigh on the business. It also expects incremental cost headwinds to make fiscal 2027 a challenging year for margin expansion.

data.title: ABB considers robotics listing if sale to SoftBank fails, sources say
data.description:
Key points:
  • Companies work to restructure $5.4 billion deal by carving out China business, people familiar say
  • ABB could spin off robotics unit or sell it to another party, sources say
  • Sides hope for solution in coming weeks but talks could run until new year, one source says

By Anousha Sakoui, Oliver Hirt and John Revill

Swiss engineering company ABB is considering a listing of its robotics unit if it cannot salvage its $5.4 billion sale to Japanese investor SoftBank after China blocked the transaction, two people with knowledge of the situation said.

Beijing blocked the sale due to concerns over SoftBank's ties with Western companies including OpenAI, in which the Japanese firm is a major investor, and risks sensitive data could be transferred to the US, Reuters previously reported.

ABB and SoftBank are working to restructure the deal to save it, potentially by carving out the Chinese business, which accounts for about 30% of the robotics unit, and selling it to a Chinese company or listing it, the people said.

Failing that, ABB would spin off the robotics unit or sell to another party, the people said.

Discussions of a spin-off have not previously been reported. Reuters could not determine what venue would be used for a listing or what value would be sought for the business in a spin-off.

SoftBank may be liable for a break fee, the terms of which have not been disclosed, one of the people said.

The preference of both ABB and SoftBank would be to rescue the deal, however, said the people, who both spoke on condition of anonymity.

The two sides are hoping to reach a solution in the coming weeks but talks could drag into next year, one of the people said.

ABB declined to comment. It has previously said it was in close dialogue and working constructively with SoftBank on the transaction after it was blocked. SoftBank declined to comment.

CHINA SCRUTINISING FOREIGN INVESTMENT AS AI RACE HEATS UP

Beijing is scrutinising foreign investment involving frontier technologies more closely as the race to dominate AI development with the United States heats up.

The decision by China's state planner not to allow the ABB unit's sale to SoftBank marked the second major deal this year to be blocked by China after Meta was ordered to unwind its more than $2 billion acquisition of AI startup Manus in April.

If the sale of the ABB division fails, it would also deal a setback to SoftBank's ambitions in robotics, which Chief Executive Masayoshi Son has highlighted as pivotal to the group's AI investment strategy.

China is ABB's largest robotics market. The Swiss group operates about 30 local companies there with 15,000 employees located in nearly 130 cities.

According to its website, ABB Engineering (Shanghai) houses the company's global robotics headquarters and is an important research-and-development centre and production base for ABB Group.

data.title: TSX eyes biggest weekly fall in over 4 years as miners drag
data.description:
Canada's main stock index fell on Friday and was on track for its steepest weekly decline in over four years, as lower metal prices weighed on miners, while investors assessed domestic retail sales data.

The S&P/TSX Composite Index was down 0.71% at 33,786.80 points by 10:43 a.m. ET (1543 GMT), eyeing its sharpest weekly drop since June 2022.

  • The materials sector , which includes miners, fell 2.6%, among the worst-hit sectors on the TSX, as precious metal prices declined. Gold slid to a more than one-year low after expectations of a hawkish US Federal Reserve boosted the dollar, while spot silver shed 2.2%

  • “Unfortunately, gold is not acting like the hedge it should in this environment. It’s been acting more like a risk-on trade,” said Sadiq Adatia, chief investment officer, BMO Global Asset Management

  • Heavyweight financials (.SPTTFS) were also down 1.2%, weighing on the index

  • Canadian retail sales rose 0.8% in September to C$75.31 billion ($52.58 billion) on a monthly basis, slightly above expectations, helped by higher sales at gasoline stations and fuel vendors

  • The energy sector was muted, with oil prices on track for a weekly decline on strong Middle East exports despite attacks on Riyadh and disruptions to tanker traffic in the Strait of Hormuz

  • Canadian technology shares shed 2.9% with Celestica and BlackBerry sliding 13.1% and 4.7%, respectively

  • Five of the TSX's 10 major sectors traded lower

  • On Wall Street, the Nasdaq fell more than 2% at the open as Anthropic tumbled after its blockbuster debut on Thursday

  • Separately, Canada is still seeking a temporary deal to ease US tariffs on its goods, though Washington has shown little willingness to budge, Trade Minister Dominic LeBlanc told an advisory committee on Thursday, two people familiar with the briefing said

data.title: Kansas City Fed Services Activity Index Falls in November
data.description:
By Colin Kellaher

Services activity in the middle of the U.S. slowed in November, while expectations for future activity moved higher, according to a monthly survey by the Federal Reserve Bank of Kansas City.

The Tenth District Services Survey's composite index, a weighted average of indexes covering revenue/sales, employment and inventory, came in at 3 in November, down from 10 in October but up from 0 in September. Readings above zero indicate expansion, while those below zero indicate contraction.

The Kansas City Fed said growth eased in both business and consumer services, driven by modest declines in auto and real-estate services.

The bank said its index of expectations for future services activity came in at 20 in November, up from 4 in October.

The Kansas City Fed's survey, released Friday, includes participants from such service industries as retail and wholesale trade, automobile dealers, real estate and restaurants. The survey provides information on current services activity in the Tenth District, which includes Colorado, Oklahoma, Wyoming, Nebraska, Kansas, the northern half of New Mexico and the western third of Missouri.

The bank's monthly manufacturing survey, released Thursday, showed that factory activity in the central U.S. rose in November.

data.title: Colombia's 2026 fiscal deficit to surpass 7.6% of GDP, finance minister says
data.description:
Colombia's 2026 fiscal deficit will exceed 7.6% of gross domestic product, above the 7.2% set out in the country's recent budget, Finance Minister Miguel Gomez said on Friday.

"An economy fueled by public spending inevitably leads to an unsustainable situation," Gomez said during an event with the Organization for Economic Cooperation and Development (OECD) in Bogota. "Not a day goes by without this government discovering some budget shortfall."

The government has presented a fiscal reform bill to Congress seeking to cut spending and increase tax revenue starting next year in an effort to shore up its deteriorating public finances.

data.title: Buckle Posts Higher 3Q Sales, Profit Slips — Update
data.description:
By Connor Hart

Buckle reported higher sales in the latest quarter, though profit edged lower.

The apparel retailer on Friday posted a fiscal third-quarter profit of $48 million, or 94 cents a share, compared with $48.7 million, or 96 cents a share, a year earlier.

Net sales climbed 2.6% to $329.2 million, benefiting from a 0.6% gain in comparable-store sales.

Shares gained 7.6%, to $44.96, on pace for their largest percentage increase since April 2025. Despite today's gains the stock has lost nearly 17% of its value year to date.

Online sales decreased 1.4%, to $52.2 million. Cost of sales increased 2.9%, to $171.9 million.
